rows.description: You keep saying one more month while the evidence says otherwise. Sunk-cost pride masks fear of quitting. Set kill criteria in advance, ask a trusted outsider to review the numbers, and choose an ending rather than a drift.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, fear, gratitude, guilt, loyalty, resentment
related mind states: fear, pride, detachment, trust

rows.description: A bigger competitor copies your product and undercuts prices. Feel the anger, then focus on customers you serve better and what cannot be copied. Complaining publicly or trashing rivals rarely helps; sharper focus might.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, fear, gratitude, guilt, loyalty, resentment

rows.description: A mentor stays with you through a dark quarter without promising a rescue. Thank them specifically, listen to hard truths, and update them on outcomes. Gratitude lasts when you use their advice, not just praise it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, fear, guilt, loyalty, resentment, rivalry

rows.description: A client changes scope repeatedly and blames you, so you feel furious. Mature response: pause, reply in writing, restate agreed scope, price extras, and keep professionalism. Venting on their staff or ghosting harms your name.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: exploitation, fear, indifference, loyalty, manipulation, protectiveness

rows.description: A client who pays on time, gives clear briefs and credits your work makes the job a pleasure. Reciprocate with reliability and honesty about limits. Good relationships are built by both sides keeping small promises.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, exploitation, fear, indifference, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: Endless free revisions, delayed payments and vague promises of future work signal exploitation. It is not your failing. Set contracts, milestones and advance payments, and be ready to end the engagement politely.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, fear, indifference, loyalty, manipulation, protectiveness

rows.description: You fear losing a big client, so you say yes to everything. Overpromising wrecks quality and health. Learn to say what is possible, give timelines you can keep, and diversify clients over time.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, exploitation, indifference, loyalty, manipulation, protectiveness

rows.description: A client hints at bad reviews or withholding payment unless you do extra. Recognise the leverage play, keep evidence, stay courteous but firm, and use formal channels. Do not give in to threats or retaliate with your own.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, exploitation, fear, indifference, loyalty, protectiveness

rows.description: An early client supported you, and now their needs outgrow your ability. Honest loyalty means telling them about the gap and helping them find better options, rather than bluffing or letting quality slip.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, exploitation, fear, indifference, manipulation, protectiveness

rows.description: A client is rude to your junior. Step in privately, set boundaries on tone, and back your teammate publicly. Ignoring it to keep the client teaches the team that respect is negotiable.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, exploitation, fear, indifference, loyalty, manipulation
